skill.name: circuit-breaker
skill.description: Implement the circuit breaker pattern to prevent cascade failures in distributed systems. Use when adding resilience to API clients, external service calls, or any operation that can fail and should fail fast.

generated_query: I'm building a microservice that depends on an external payment gateway API. The API is sometimes slow or returns 5xx errors, and when it does, my entire service starts timing out and the problem cascades. I need to add a resilience layer that will "fail fast" after a few consecutive failures, wait a while before retrying, and only allow traffic again after the external service has recovered. Also, I want to return a cached or default response while the circuit is open so the rest of my application doesn't break. Can you implement this pattern in TypeScript (or Python) for my payment client? I'll pass a function that calls the external API, and I want the circuit breaker to track the state automatically. For testing, I'll simulate 4 failures with a mock function, then wait 10 seconds, and verify that the circuit allows a successful call after that. The circuit should open after 3 failures, stay open for at least 10 seconds, then go to half-open and close after 2 consecutive successes. Also provide a fallback that returns `{ status: 'unavailable', retryAfter: 10 }` when the circuit is open.
